summary: 镜子既能用来研究自我意识，也能改变人的行为。对动物自我识别、人的外貌判断和镜像大小的实验表明，我们对镜子显示的东西常有错误的直觉。
logic: 观察镜前行为和自我识别
人怎样看待自己的面孔
检验关于镜像大小的直觉

paragraphs.brief: 无论是高抛光金属制成的还是玻璃制成的，背面涂有金属，镜子已经吸引人们数千年。
sentences: Whether made of highly polished metal or of glass with a coating of metal on the back, mirrors have fascinated people for thousands of years.
无论是高抛光金属制成的还是玻璃制成的，背面涂有金属，镜子已经吸引人们数千年。
Ancient Egyptians were often depicted holding hand mirrors.
古埃及人经常被描绘成手镜子。
For centuries, the people of Rajasthan in India have sewn bits of reflective glass into their clothing, and the resulting sparkle emphasizes the magic and mystery of that desert land.
几个世纪以来，印度的拉贾斯坦邦人民把反射玻璃缝在衣服上，由此产生的闪光突出了沙漠的神奇和神秘。

paragraphs.brief: 对科学家来说，镜像的简单性和复杂性使得它们能够有效和方便地探索关于人类和其他“智慧”物种的认知和认知问题，以及大脑如何解释和运用外部世界的大量感官信息。
sentences: To scientists, the simultaneous simplicity and complexity of mirrors make them effective and accessible tools for exploring questions about perception and cognition in humans and other 'intelligent' species, and about how the brain interprets and acts upon the great mass of sensory information from the external world.
对科学家来说，镜像的简单性和复杂性使得它们能够有效和方便地探索关于人类和其他“智慧”物种的认知和认知问题，以及大脑如何解释和运用外部世界的大量感官信息。

Mirrors are used to study how the brain decides what is self and what is other, how it judges distance, and how it reconstructs the richly three-dimensional quality of the outside world from what is essentially a two-dimensional snapshot taken by the retina of the eye.
镜像用来研究大脑如何决定什么是自我，什么是其他，如何判断距离，以及它如何从眼睛视网膜所拍摄的两维截图中重建外部世界的丰富三维质量。
Mirrors are applied in medicine to create reflected images of patients' limbs or other body parts and thus trick the brain into healing itself.
镜像被应用到医学中来制作病人肢体或其他身体部位的反射图像从而诱使大脑自我治愈
Mirror therapy has been successful in treating chronic pain and paralysis.
镜像疗法成功地治疗了慢性疼痛和麻痹。
In a sense, mirrors are the best 'virtual reality' system that can be built.
从某种意义上说，镜子是最好的“虚拟现实”系统。
The object 'inside' the mirror is virtual, but as far as our eyes are concerned, it exists as much as any other object.
镜子的“ 内侧” 是虚拟的，但就我们的眼睛而言，它的存在与任何其他物体一样多。

paragraphs.brief: 研究表明，镜像可以暗中影响人类的行为，往往以令人惊讶的积极方式。
sentences: Research has shown that mirrors can subtly affect human behaviour, often in surprisingly positive ways.
研究表明，镜像可以暗中影响人类的行为，往往以令人惊讶的积极方式。
Subjects tested in a room with a mirror have been found to work harder and to be less inclined to cheat, compared with control groups performing the same exercises in non-mirrored settings.
与在非幻影环境中进行相同练习的控制组相比，在有镜子的房间测试的实验对象发现工作更努力，更不愿意作弊。

In addition, the researchers found that people in a room with a mirror were comparatively less likely to make judgements about others based on negative social stereotypes concerning, for example, sex, race or religion.
此外，研究人员发现，有镜子的房间里的人比较不可能根据诸如性别、种族或宗教等消极的社会定型观念来判断其他人。
The researchers said that this indicates that when people are made to be self-aware, they are likelier to stop and think about what they are doing.
研究人员说，这表明当人们被培养为自我意识时，他们更愿意停下来，思考自己在做什么。
A by-product of that awareness may be a shift away from acting on autopilot toward more desirable ways of behaving.
这种认识的副产品可能是从自动驾驶转向更可取的行为方式。
Physical self-reflection, in other words, encourages philosophical self-reflection — a lesson in the ancient Greek notion that you cannot know or appreciate others until you know yourself.
自我反省，换句话说，鼓励哲学自我反省——这是古希腊概念中的一个教训，在认识自己之前，你无法了解或欣赏他人。

paragraphs.brief: 自我意识与周密的社会性之间的联系可能有助于解释为什么在镜子中被发现承认自己身份的少数非人类物种是那些具有复杂社会生活的物种。
sentences: The link between self-awareness and elaborate sociality may help explain why the few nonhuman species that have been found to recognize themselves in a mirror are those with sophisticated social lives.
自我意识与周密的社会性之间的联系可能有助于解释为什么在镜子中被发现承认自己身份的少数非人类物种是那些具有复杂社会生活的物种。

Animals that live in communal units, such as the great apes – chimpanzees, bonobos, orangutans and gorillas – along with dolphins and Asian elephants, have passed the famed mirror self-recognition test, which means they will, when given a mirror, scrutinize marks that have been applied to their faces or bodies.
生活在社区单位的动物，如大猩猩(黑猩猩、大猩猩、猩猩和大猩猩)以及海豚和亚洲大象，都通过了著名的镜像自我识别测试，这意味着当给它们照镜子时，它们会仔细检查在它们脸上或身体上贴过标记。
The animals will also check up on personal cleanliness, inspecting their mouths, nostrils and bodies.
动物们还会检查个人是否干净，检查他们的口腔、鼻孔和身体。
Yet not all members of self-reflective species will pass the mirror test.
但并非所有自我反射的物种成员都会通过镜像测试。
Studies of individual elephants and dolphins raised in isolation suggest that these particular individuals do not exhibit mirror self-recognition.
对单独养大的大象和海豚的研究显示，这些特定的个人并不表现出镜像的自我承认。

paragraphs.brief: 因此，人类不一定看到镜子中的样子，实际上也是这样。
sentences: For that matter, humans do not necessarily see the face in the mirror as it actually is either.
因此，人类不一定看到镜子中的样子，实际上也是这样。
What the human eye sees objectively and how the brain interprets that image are not necessarily the same.
人类眼睛客观地看什么以及大脑如何解释这个形象不一定是一样的

Dr Nicholas Epley, Professor of Behavioral Science at the University of Chicago, USA, described experiments in which people were asked to pick out pictures of themselves from among pictures of other human faces.
美国芝加哥大学行为学教授Nicholas Epley博士描述了人们被要求从其他人类面孔照片中挑选自己照片的实验。

Participants identified their personal photographs significantly quicker when their faces had been computer-enhanced to be more appealing and they were likely to call this retouched image their genuine face.
参加者发现，当他们的脸部在计算机上得到加强，更吸引人时，他们的个人照片就明显更快了，而且他们可能把这一被改过自新的照片称为真实的图像。

This self-delusion is not simply the result of a widespread preference for prettiness: when asked to match photographs of strangers, participants were, in fact, best at spotting unenhanced faces — that is, those not made to look prettier.
这种自我淡化不仅仅是普遍偏爱美貌的结果：当被要求将陌生人的照片相匹配时，与会者实际上最擅长发现未增强的面孔——即那些不美的面孔。

paragraphs.brief: 人们通常会为自身利益解决这些多重形象的问题。
sentences: How can we be so self-delusional when the truth stares back at us?
当真相重现时我们怎么能如此自欺欺人呢？
Dr Epley explains that, although we do indeed see ourselves in the mirror every day, we don't look exactly the same every time.
埃普利博士解释说，虽然我们确实每天都在镜子里看到自己，但我们的外表并不完全一样。
There is the just-out-of-bed morning you, the ready-for-work you, the dressed-for-an-elegant-dinner you.
刚从床上出来，你，准备工作，穿衣为 - 一个人 - 吃饭。
Which image is you?
你是什么图案？
People on average resolve the question of these multiple images of themselves in their favour.
人们通常会为自身利益解决这些多重形象的问题。
That is, they piece together a mental representation formed from different aspects of themselves when they are looking their best.
也就是说，当他们表现得最好时，他们从不同的方面形成了精神上的表达。

paragraphs.brief: 第一个问题是，人们压倒性地说，“镜子上我的脸的轮廓与我的脸差不多大。
sentences: In a series of other studies, psychologists interviewed people about what they think a mirror shows them.
心理学家在一系列其他研究中采访了人们关于他们认为镜子向他们展示的东西
They asked questions like, 'Imagine you are standing in front of a bathroom mirror; how big do you think the image of your face is on the surface?
他们问道：“想象你站在浴室的镜子前，你觉得你的脸像在表面有多大？
And what will happen to the size of that image if you step steadily backward, away from the glass?'
如果你从玻璃上往后退一步，那图像的大小会怎样呢？”
To the first question, people overwhelmingly say 'The outline of my face on the mirror would be pretty much the size of my face.
第一个问题是，人们压倒性地说，“镜子上我的脸的轮廓与我的脸差不多大。
As for the second question, that's obvious: if I move away from the mirror, the size of my image will shrink with each step.'
至于第二个问题，这是显而易见的：如果我离开镜子，我的形象的大小会随着每一步而缩小。
Both answers, it turns out, are wrong.
事实证明，这两个答案都是错误的。
Outline your face on a mirror, and you will find it to be exactly half the size of your real face.
用镜子来概括一下你的脸你就会发现你的脸有你真实脸的一半大小
Step back as much as you please, and the size of that outlined oval will not change: it remains half the size of your face, even as the background scene reflected in the mirror steadily changes.
尽量往后退，所描述的奥瓦尔的大小不会改变：它仍然是你脸的一半大小，即使镜子中反映的背景场景在稳步变化。

items.en: The conflicting nature of mirrors makes them inappropriate aids for investigating human thought.
items.zh: 镜像的矛盾性质使得它们不适合用来调查人类思想。
items.why: 镜子既简单又复杂；作者认为正是这个特点使它成为研究感知和认知的有效工具，与题干所说“不适合”相反。

items.en: Humans find it difficult to distinguish between reflections of two- and three-dimensional objects.
items.zh: 人类发现很难区分二维和三维物体的反射。
items.why: 镜子能帮助研究者考察大脑怎样从二维输入重建三维感知。它没有说明人是否难以区分二维和三维物体的镜像。

items.en: Illusions using mirrors can help in the treatment of medical problems.
items.zh: 使用镜子的幻觉可以帮助治疗医疗问题。
items.why: 原文写道“镜像疗法成功地治疗了慢性疼痛和麻痹”，支持题干所说的“使用镜子的幻觉可以帮助治疗医疗问题”。

items.en: Mirrors for use in scientific experiments have to be constructed to precise specifications.
items.zh: 用于科学实验的镜像必须按照精确的规格建造。
items.why: 原文称镜子是研究感知和认知的有效工具。关于使用价值的评价，没有附带实验用镜的制造精度或规格要求。

correct: realise that the marks they see are on their own body.

items.zh: 下列哪一个标题最适合第三篇阅读文章？

items.zh: Epley医生发现当识别自己的图像时
items.answer: H · locate the photographs faster if they are made to look attractive.
items.solution: 如果照片看起来有吸引力的话找得更快

items.zh: Epley博士在试图识别不熟悉个人的照片时发现,
items.answer: F · select those photographs which have not been altered.

items.zh: Epley医生说，一个客观的反思是不可能的，因为人们

items.solution: 每天都在各种情况下面对他们的形象。

items.zh: 埃普利医生说，当形成一种观点他们如何看待他们的样子,

items.zh: 当人们从近距离猜测他们镜子脸的大小时
items.answer: E · estimate the image to be larger than it actually is.
items.solution: 估计图像的大小大于实际的大小。

items.zh: 当他们想象从镜子后退的时候

items.solution: 假设他们的形象会逐渐变小

pairs: 第 3 段 · 第 6 句
points: 原文称镜子是研究感知和认知的有效工具。关于使用价值的评价，没有附带实验用镜的制造精度或规格要求。
题干问“当他们想象从镜子后退的时候”。定位句写到“至于第二个问题，这是显而易见的：如果我离开镜子，我的形象的大小会随着每一步而缩小”。
clauses: …, mirrors have fascinated people for thousands of years.
连接词 whether 引出“Whether made of highly polished metal or of glass with a coating of metal on the back”，说明主句的选择关系。
先读主句的动作，再用 whether 把这一层关系补进去。
“that mirrors can subtly affect human behaviour, often in surprisingly positive ways”补足 shown 的内容，交代究竟在说、判断或发现什么。
先读 shown 所在的主句，再把 that 后面的内容作为一个整体。
